standard.title: Communicating
standard.description: write and create texts to communicate observations, findings and ideas, using everyday and scientific vocabulary
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can share ideas informally (F band). They now begin to create texts — written, drawn, modelled or role-played — that communicate observations and ideas using both everyday and scientific vocabulary.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students write and create texts to communicate science observations and ideas, using scientific vocabulary alongside everyday language and selecting from a range of forms (drawing, model, label, role-play, sequential representation).

nodes.label: Texts communicate science observations using scientific vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create a text (written, drawn, modelled or performed) that communicates a science observation or idea, using at least two science vocabulary terms correctly.
nodes.minimum_width: Students create a text communicating a science observation and use at least two science vocabulary terms.
nodes.typical_width: Students explore the difference between everyday and scientific vocabulary; create models, drawings, labels, arrows or role-plays to represent observations (habitats, seasonal changes, force effects); represent sequential changes using drawings or photographs; and describe their representations using both everyday and scientific vocabulary.
wider: Acknowledge and learn about First Nations Australians' ways of representing and sharing observations — examining diverse communication forms for scientific knowledge
Represent push and pull forces using role-play, labels, arrows or time-lapse drawings — applying multiple representation forms to the same concept
Role-play or recount how people use patterns to make predictions at work or in daily life (AC9S1H01)
success_criteria: Creates a text communicating a science observation in at least one form (drawing, model, labels, role-play)
Uses at least two science vocabulary terms correctly in the text
